basis: Retinal racemose hemangioma is a retinal arteriovenous malformation, directly involving the eye and its vessels; isolated disease does not imply CNS involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: this is an arteriovenous malformation of retinal vessels; arteries and veins fall within the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Valve disease and intellectual disability define the syndrome; structural eyelid dysfunction from ptosis occurs in 30-79%. Short stature and delayed bone age alone do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis is structural eyelid dysfunction reported in 30-79%, meeting the supplied frequency threshold.

basis: Inherited lymphoma susceptibility specifies future risk, without established lymphoma, blood-cell disease or immune dysfunction.

decisions.haematologic: none: susceptibility to a blood malignancy does not establish existing blood-cell or marrow disease.

basis: Neurodegeneration and skeletal hypoplasia define disease; low IgG 2/4 with recurrent infections 4/4 supports immunodeficiency. Leukopenia/lymphopenia affects 3/4; hepatomegaly alone lacks injury evidence.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: immunodeficiency is supported by low IgG in 2/4, lymphopenia in 3/4 and recurrent infections in 4/4; the mechanism axis applies.

basis: Splenic congestion with blood-cell destruction and pancytopenia defines the concept. Underlying portal hypertension or cirrhosis is a separate condition, not organ damage caused by splenomegaly.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: portal hypertension is an underlying, separately diagnosed cause of splenic congestion; the definition does not establish an intrinsic vascular disorder.

basis: 45,X Turner phenotype with gonadal failure; congenital cardiac defects ~30-50%, renal anomalies ~30-40%, and intrinsic hearing loss >30% over life. Additional skeletal features omitted at cap.

decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss directly reflects cochlear dysfunction and affects more than 30% over the typical lifetime course.

basis: Renovascular hypertension is defined by renal arterial disease with impaired kidney perfusion driving hypertension; established renal parenchymal injury is not required for the primary renal axis.

decisions.renal: primary: impaired renal perfusion and kidney-mediated hypertension define the disease, supported by its renal hypertension and kidney disorder ancestry.

basis: Complex III deficiency causes metabolic crises. Pancreatitis in 1/2 is a separately diagnosed complication; vomiting and episodic confusion do not establish lasting gastrointestinal or neurologic damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: pancreatitis in 1/2 meets the numerical threshold but is a separately diagnosed complication; vomiting and diarrhea alone do not establish direct organ damage.

basis: DNAJB11 disease causes renal cysts and progressive renal dysfunction. Hepatic cysts occur in 9/20 (45%), but impairing hepatic involvement is unestablished; hypertension is separately diagnosed.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic cysts occur in 45%, but the evidence does not establish liver injury, impaired function or clinically significant cystic occupation.

basis: Tumor originates in autonomic neuroendocrine paraganglia; nonsecretory status does not change its origin. Catecholamine-related HPO entries contradict the definition and cannot support additional axes.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: paraganglia are neuroendocrine organs; a nonfunctioning tumor retains its endocrine tissue of origin despite lacking catecholamine secretion.
